chunks: Yunus narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The thief's hand is not cut off except for something whose value reaches a mijann, and that is one-quarter of a dinar.

key_terms.دِينَارٍ: Dinar, a gold coin used as a currency standard
key_terms.مِجَنّاً: A mijann, a specific unit of weight/value for silver
key_terms.يُقطَعُ: Is cut off (referring to the hand)

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum value of stolen goods required for hadd al-sariqah (cutting the hand) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the nisab for hadd al-sariqah, specifying that the stolen item must be worth at least a mijann (one-quarter of a dinar) to warrant amputation. This threshold reflects the scholarly consensus on the minimum value of currency or goods that demonstrates significant loss, ensuring the punishment is applied only to substantial thefts rather than minor infractions.
